Vendor profile

Dassault Systèmes

Dassault Systèmes

By Gstarcademy Editorial Team Last reviewed 2026-06-23 Editorial process

Company Overview

Dassault Systemes SE is a French multinational software company headquartered in Velizy-Villacoublay, near Paris. Founded in 1981 as a spinoff from Dassault Aviation, the company develops the 3DEXPERIENCE platform and a portfolio of industry-leading CAD/PLM applications including CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, SIMULIA, DELMIA, and ENOVIA.

Dassault Systemes serves aerospace, automotive, consumer goods, life sciences, and industrial equipment markets. The company's strategy centers on the "virtual twin experience" — creating comprehensive digital replicas of products, processes, and even human bodies for design optimization and simulation.

Core Brands

  • CATIA: High-end 3D CAD for complex surface modeling, multi-discipline design, and systems engineering — dominant in aerospace and automotive.
  • SOLIDWORKS: Mid-market parametric 3D CAD with the largest installed base in mechanical engineering — acquired in 1997, operates as an independent subsidiary.
  • SIMULIA: Simulation portfolio including Abaqus FEA, CST electromagnetics, and Tosca optimization.
  • ENOVIA: Product lifecycle management (PLM) for configuration management, change control, and regulatory compliance.

SOLIDWORKS

Dassault Systèmes' mainstream parametric MCAD — feature-based modelling, assembly mates, and 2D drawings tightly coupled to the 3D model.

Market Position & Strategy

Dassault Systèmes (3DS) occupies the premium tier of the CAD/PLM market, with CATIA as its flagship for complex product design (automotive, aerospace) and the 3DEXPERIENCE platform as its strategic vehicle for cloud transformation. The company's acquisition strategy—buying SolidWorks (1997), SIMULIA (Abaqus, 2005), GEOVIA, BIOVIA, and Medidata—expanded its reach from mechanical CAD into life sciences, mining, and clinical trials.

The 3DEXPERIENCE platform strategy aims to create a unified data backbone connecting design (CATIA), simulation (SIMULIA), manufacturing (DELMIA), and collaboration (ENOVIA) in a single cloud environment. For practitioners, this means increasingly tight integration between previously separate tools, but also vendor lock-in as workflows depend on the 3DEXPERIENCE infrastructure.

SolidWorks remains Dassault's volume product, serving the mainstream mechanical design market. The introduction of SolidWorks Cloud (3DEXPERIENCE SolidWorks) represents a potential long-term migration path, though desktop SolidWorks continues to receive active development and retains its large installed base.

Technology Platform

Dassault's technology foundation rests on the CGM (Convergent Geometric Modeler) kernel, which powers CATIA, SolidWorks, and SIMULIA. CGM handles both B-rep solid modeling and polyhedral (mesh) geometry in a unified framework—a capability that becomes increasingly important as additive manufacturing and reverse engineering workflows require mixing scanned mesh data with precise parametric geometry.

CATIA V5/V6 introduced the feature-based parametric modeling paradigm that now dominates the industry. The V6 architecture moved from file-based data management to a database-centric model (ENOVIA-backed), where every design element is a database object with full version history and access control. This architectural choice trades file portability for enterprise-grade data management.

The 3DEXPERIENCE platform runs on a multi-tenant cloud architecture (available on AWS and private cloud deployments) that provides browser-based access to CAD tools through CATIA on the Cloud and SolidWorks Cloud. The cloud rendering and computation capabilities enable thin-client access, though network latency can impact the interactive modeling experience compared to native desktop applications.

Learning Resources

  • 3DEXPERIENCE Edu: Official learning platform with role-based training paths covering CATIA, SolidWorks, SIMULIA, and DELMIA.
  • MySolidWorks Training: SolidWorks-specific training with structured courses, practice exercises, and certification preparation.
  • CATIA Companion: In-product tutorials and guided workflows for CATIA on the 3DEXPERIENCE platform.
  • Certification: CSWA (Certified SolidWorks Associate) and CSWP (Professional) certifications are widely recognized in mechanical engineering hiring. CATIA certifications are available through 3DEXPERIENCE Edu.
